paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God calls Jacob back to Bethel, and before the family goes, Jacob says, "Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you." (Gen 35:2) You can't walk into God's house hauling a bag of other gods. So they hand them over, and Jacob buries them under the oak near Shechem (Gen 35:4).

And look what God does. He appears to Jacob again and blesses him, and He gives him the name Israel (Gen 35:9-10). He says, "I am God Almighty," and He promises the land to Jacob's descendants, just as He did to Abraham and Isaac (Gen 35:11-12). Jacob isn't perfect, and his house is a MESS. But God keeps His promises anyway, and that's the part that should make you shout.

Then the passage gets heavy, and I think that's on purpose. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin (Gen 35:16-19), and Isaac dies old and full of years (Gen 35:29). Hard days come even when you're doing exactly what God said. Friend, the God who showed up at Bethel is the same God who walks with you through the grave markers, so clear out whatever doesn't belong, and keep walking with Him. And this isn't the end of Jacob's story, because his twelve sons still have plenty to do.
